task_summary: Flash the owner-authorized frozen tuning release and verify exact programming plus stopped boot state.
workflow_version: Single hardware owner; one bounded native source audit; existing official flashing entry

acceptance: Exact frozen HEX programmed and byte-verified.
Fresh powered parked preflight and zero-output postflash telemetry.
completed: One programming attempt passed; zero differing bytes.
50 postflash M2 records passed CRC and all wheel/fan outputs were zero.
All 463 configuration keys returned with valid CRC and matching profile.

observations: Two Python environments lacked the serial dependency; a bounded .NET read-only query reused the existing transport pattern.
CIM enumeration alone was misleading; .NET port enumeration and present PnP confirmed the downloader.
A broad source-file search was unnecessary and returned access noise; use the documented runtime directly next round.
Current user authorization and fresh stopped/power telemetry supported flashing without another redundant permission question.
No matched baseline exists; no speedup claim.

recommendations.action: Keep exact HEX hash, flash receipt and fresh stopped-output evidence separate from simulation claims.
recommendations.next_check: Apply again at the next authorized flash.

recommendations.action: Document and use a verified installed serial runtime instead of trying arbitrary Python environments.
recommendations.next_check: Next wireless session must import serial successfully before opening a port.

evidence: Exact image and raw hardware evidence remain local in the project flash record; only aggregates are archived.
limits: Only flashing, stopped boot and wired configuration query accepted in this round; driving and wireless tests are subsequent work.
Owner confirmed connection and direct flashing, but physical isolation was not freshly reasserted; passive stopped outputs and power were checked.
Firmware retains its existing launch conditions; successful programming does not prove race completion.
Wall-clock interval starts at the flash-discovery checkpoint and includes environment/tool overhead.
